newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IG Metall warns of large protests Thursday.
newsitem.headline: German IG Metall warns of large protests Thursday.

text.p: German trade union IG Metall warned of large protests to be held on Thursday by engineering workers over planned cuts to benefits following the collapse of talks on the issue with the Gesamtmetall employers federation.

"It will be a big day," IG Metall chairman Klaus Zwickel told journalists on Wednesday after 20 hours of negotiations between it and engineering employers had failed to produce any agreement over pay and future conditions in the sector.

IG Metall earlier this month organised stoppages involving over 100,000 workers at factories around the country after a number of firms said they would implement a new law cutting sick pay to 80 percent of salary from the current 100 percent.
Disruption caused by this and earlier protests cost giant Daimler-Benz AG alone some 220 million marks in lost production.

Daimler and others later said they would be postponing the planned sick cuts in an effort to reach wider agreement with workers on the issue. A 20 percent cut in sick pay could save German firms up to 12 billion marks annually in labour costs.

But Gesamtmetall president Werner Stumpfe said that in sector-wide talks with IG Metall the trade union was not prepared to negotiate on sick pay. He said whether firms sought to introduce sick pay cuts or not would now be up to them.
